evidence.finding: Tasks can be pinned in the agent Command Center.

evidence.title: Codex release rust-v0.163.0
evidence.locator: New Features and Bug Fixes
evidence.finding: /config searches preferences. Follow-ups steer a running turn; interrupting stops Code Mode cells and nested tool calls. /daemon restarts the background server, warns about interruptible work and reconnects. /keymap configures a leader key.

evidence.title: Codex release rust-v0.164.0
evidence.locator: New Features and Bug Fixes
evidence.finding: Enterprise MCP can authenticate with Codex account grants. Credentials are masked in supported remote Bash and Zsh sessions. Viewed and generated images preview in the transcript. Failed compaction leaves no partial summaries.

evidence.title: Codex release rust-v0.165.0
evidence.locator: New Features and Bug Fixes
evidence.finding: The session picker gets a repository filter and the command center directory grouping across linked worktrees. Reasoning effort can change mid-conversation by default. Memory v2 is the default for fresh profiles. Dropped remote MCP tool requests are cancelled.

evidence.title: Codex release rust-v0.166.0
evidence.locator: New Features and Bug Fixes
evidence.finding: Unarchiving a parent restores spawned descendant threads. Safety blocks explain themselves and offer safer follow-ups. codex queue --resume resumes unloaded threads.

evidence.title: Codex release rust-v0.167.0
evidence.locator: New Features; Changelog #58161, #57866, #58129
evidence.finding: The command center and session picker mark unread results. Patch details expand during approval. Changelog: MCP approval metadata includes tool names and annotation hints (#58161); transient environment startup failures retry on the next turn (#57866); subagent relationships persist (#58129).

evidence.title: Codex release rust-v0.169.0
evidence.locator: New Features and Bug Fixes
evidence.finding: Older tasks can be searched from the agent command center.

evidence.title: Codex release rust-v0.171.0
evidence.locator: New Features and Bug Fixes
evidence.finding: The TUI workspace is on by default, showing subagent transcripts alongside the main conversation.

evidence.title: openai/codex releases
evidence.locator: Release list; tag rust-v0.171.0
evidence.finding: Stable releases rust-v0.157.0 (2026-09-25) through rust-v0.171.0 (2026-11-20, marked Latest; tag commit ccf9be8), with 0.173.0 alphas through 2026-11-21.

evidence.title: Codex Cloud
evidence.locator: Why use Codex Cloud; Getting started
evidence.finding: Cloud tasks can use repositories from a connected GitHub or GitLab account; users review changed files and checks, request follow-up changes in the same chat, and commit or open a pull request.

evidence.title: Codex Cloud (Legacy) environments
evidence.locator: page title; Environment variables and secrets
evidence.finding: The page is titled Codex Cloud (Legacy), which still serves Code Review and the Linear and GitHub integrations, and points to a newer Cloud environments guide; no end date is given. Secrets are available only to setup scripts and are removed before the agent phase.

evidence.title: Codex pricing
evidence.locator: usage-limit estimates table and footnotes
evidence.finding: Plus and Business show estimated local messages per five-hour period, Pro has no five-hour limit, cloud tasks may use more allowance, and weekly limits may apply; these are estimates, not fixed limits.

evidence.title: Codex protocol ApprovalsReviewer
evidence.locator: enum ApprovalsReviewer (#[default] User; AutoReview serialized auto_review, alias guardian_subagent) and its doc comment; tag rust-v0.171.0 (commit ccf9be8)
evidence.finding: Approval requests (sandbox escapes, blocked network access, MCP approval prompts, ARC escalations) are routed to the user by default; automatic review by a prompted subagent applies only when approvals_reviewer is set to auto_review.

evidence.title: Codex config MemoriesToml
evidence.locator: struct MemoriesToml, field version doc comment; tag rust-v0.171.0 (commit ccf9be8)
evidence.finding: The memory pipeline version setting says fresh profiles default to v2 when memories are enabled (unless dual-write is explicitly disabled), and existing v1 profiles default to v1.

evidence.title: Codex pricing: usage limits
evidence.locator: usage-limit estimates introduction and footnotes below the table
evidence.finding: The five-hour estimates cover Plus and Standard Business; Pro plans currently have no five-hour limit; weekly limits may also apply; Enterprise/Edu users with flexible pricing have no fixed rate limits and usage scales with credits, while Enterprise and Edu plans without flexible pricing have the same per-seat limits as Plus for most features.

evidence.title: Codex rust-v0.172.0 analytics config
evidence.locator: config_toml.rs lines 556-559; codex-rs/core/src/otel_init.rs line 79; codex-rs/tui/src/startup_orchestration.rs line 703
evidence.finding: analytics.enabled=false 'disables OpenAI analytics across Codex product surfaces on this machine'; unset falls back to the client default, which the TUI passes as true.
